Value Algebra Without Leaving Note¶

The operator surface lets ordinary C++ expressions build text and Boolean pipelines while preserving Note shape, dtype, and ownership. The symbols do not all apply to every dtype:

Expression family

Accepted dtype

Meaning

Result

left + right

matching Text or matching Bytes

concatenate paired cells

Text or Bytes Note

text * count

Text or Bytes

repeat each cell count times

same dtype and shape

comparisons

two Notes of the same dtype

compare paired lane values

Bool Note

comparison with a string

Text or Bytes Note

compare each cell with one text/byte value

Bool Note

&, `

, ^, ~`

Bool

elementwise Boolean composition

stream << note

every dtype, including undefined

write the public representation

the same stream

+ is concatenation, not numeric addition. Int64 and Float64 Notes can be compared but cannot be added through this surface. * repeats text; it is not numeric multiplication. Boolean composition uses the eager bitwise symbols because C++ logical && and || cannot return a lane-wise Note result.

Pairing And One-Element Broadcast¶

Binary Note operators accept equal shapes, or they broadcast an operand whose numel() is one across the other operand. A rank-zero Note is the clearest scalar spelling, but a one-element vector also participates in this rule. The result takes the non-singleton operand’s shape. If both operands contain one element, the left shape is retained.

There is no general singleton-axis broadcasting. Shapes [2, 1] and [1, 2] both contain two cells, but they are different shapes and neither operand has one cell, so pairing rejects them. This prevents accidental row-major pairing between structurally different Notes.

All operator results are newly allocated Notes. Text concatenation and repetition build a new packed arena because cell bytes change. Comparisons and Boolean operations allocate contiguous one-byte Bool storage. Compound assignment first computes the checked out-of-place result and then replaces the left handle; another Note sharing the old storage is not rewritten.

Undefined operands reject rather than propagating. Empty Notes are valid when their shapes satisfy the pairing rule and produce an empty result with that shape.

Concatenation¶

Example 1: Pair Two Notes Cell By Cell¶

const auto names = pluss::note::make({"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"});
const auto punctuation = pluss::note::make({"!", "?", "."});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(names + punctuation) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Ada!", "Grace?", "Linus."]

Cells pair by position. Concatenation never joins neighboring cells or changes the number of cells.

Example 2: Put A Literal On Either Side¶

const auto names = pluss::note::make({"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"});

std::cout << "suffix\n" << pluss::note::print(names + "!") << '\n';
std::cout << "prefix\n" << pluss::note::print("Dr. " + names) << '\n';

Output¶

suffix
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Ada!", "Grace!", "Linus!"]
prefix
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Dr. Ada", "Dr. Grace", "Dr. Linus"]

Operand order determines byte order. A right literal is a suffix; a left literal is a prefix.

Example 3: Broadcast A One-Element Note And Preserve Rank¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c", "d"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix + pluss::note::make("!")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a!", "b!"], 
  ["c!", "d!"]
]

The scalar contributes bytes to each cell; the matrix supplies the result geometry.

Example 4: Compound Assignment Rebinds Only The Left Handle¶

const auto original = pluss::note::make({"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"});
auto changed = original;
changed += pluss::note::make({"!", "?", "."});
changed += "#";

std::cout << "changed\n" << pluss::note::print(changed) << '\n';
std::cout << "original\n" << pluss::note::print(original) << '\n';

Output¶

changed
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Ada!#", "Grace?#", "Linus.#"]
original
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Ada", "Grace", "Linus"]

Copying a Note copies an intrusive handle. += does not mutate the shared arena; it assigns a fresh result to changed. If validation or allocation fails, that assignment does not occur.

Example 5: Bytes Stay Bytes, Including Embedded Zero Bytes¶

const auto raw = pluss::note::bytes(
    std::vector<std::string>{std::string("A\0", 2), "B"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{2});
const auto joined = raw + pluss::note::bytes("!");

std::cout << "bytes=" << std::boolalpha << joined.is_bytes()
          << " sizes=" << joined.at(0).size() << ','
          << joined.at(1).size() << '\n';

Output¶

bytes=true sizes=3,2

Concatenation is length-aware; it does not stop at an embedded zero byte. Text and Bytes cannot be mixed because that would silently assign an encoding interpretation to raw bytes.

Example 6: Empty Shapes Remain Empty¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 0});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(empty + empty) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 0], dim=2, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

Example 7: Invalid Concatenation Rejects Before A Result Is Returned¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c", "d"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});

try { (void)(matrix + pluss::note::make({"1", "2", "3", "4"})); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "shape mismatch: rejected\n"; }

try { (void)(pluss::note::make("text") + pluss::note::bytes("raw")); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "mixed encoding: rejected\n"; }

try {
  (void)(pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}) +
         pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{3, 4}));
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "native dtype: rejected\n"; }

try { (void)(pluss::note::make("x") + pluss::Note::undefined()); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "undefined: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

shape mismatch: rejected
mixed encoding: rejected
native dtype: rejected
undefined: rejected

Repetition¶

Repetition duplicates the bytes inside each cell. It does not repeat cells or axes. Therefore shape and numel() never change. Use the structural repeat or repeat_interleave when the structure rather than cell content must grow.

The count must be nonnegative. Zero produces an empty string in every existing cell. Before reserving each destination string, the implementation checks that cell_size * times fits the implementation’s maximum string size, preventing size arithmetic from wrapping.

Example 8: Multiply From Either Side¶

std::cout << "right\n"
          << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::make({"ha", "go"}) * 3) << '\n';
std::cout << "left\n"
          << pluss::note::print(2 * pluss::note::make({"ab", "x"})) << '\n';

Output¶

right
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["hahaha", "gogogo"]
left
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["abab", "xx"]

Example 9: Zero And Compound Repetition¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c", "d"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << "zero\n" << pluss::note::print(matrix * 0) << '\n';

auto chant = pluss::note::make({"na", "batman"});
chant *= 2;
std::cout << "compound\n" << pluss::note::print(chant) << '\n';

Output¶

zero
Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["", ""], 
  ["", ""]
]
compound
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["nana", "batmanbatman"]

Example 10: Repetition Failures¶

try { (void)(pluss::note::make("ha") * -1); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "negative: rejected\n"; }

try { (void)(pluss::note::make(std::vector<bool>{true, false}) * 2); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "Bool: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

negative: rejected
Bool: rejected

Comparisons¶

All six relations are elementwise and return a shape-preserving Bool Note. Note-to-Note comparison requires identical dtypes. Text and Bytes use exact unsigned bytewise lexicographic order: there is no case folding, locale-aware collation, normalization, or numeric parsing. Int64 and Float64 use native numeric order; Bool uses false < true.

Float64 follows ordinary floating-point comparison. A NaN is unequal to every value, including itself; <, <=, >, and >= are also false when either operand lane is NaN.

String operands are available only for Text and Bytes Notes. Numeric scalar comparison remains explicit: construct a rank-zero Note with the matching dtype. This avoids parsing strings or silently promoting native dtypes.

Example 11: Exercise Every Relation¶

const auto left = pluss::note::make({"a", "b", "c"});
const auto right = pluss::note::make({"a", "x", "b"});

std::cout << "==\n" << pluss::note::print(left == right) << '\n';
std::cout << "!=\n" << pluss::note::print(left != right) << '\n';
std::cout << "<\n"  << pluss::note::print(left < right) << '\n';
std::cout << "<=\n" << pluss::note::print(left <= right) << '\n';
std::cout << ">\n"  << pluss::note::print(left > right) << '\n';
std::cout << ">=\n" << pluss::note::print(left >= right) << '\n';

Output¶

==
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, false, false]
!=
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[false, true, true]
<
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[false, true, false]
<=
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, true, false]
>
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[false, false, true]
>=
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, false, true]

Example 12: Literal Orientation Changes The Question¶

const auto values = pluss::note::make({"a", "b", "c"});
std::cout << "values >= b\n" << pluss::note::print(values >= "b") << '\n';
std::cout << "b < values\n" << pluss::note::print("b" < values) << '\n';

Output¶

values >= b
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[false, true, true]
b < values
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[false, false, true]

The first expression includes equality; the second asks strictly whether the literal precedes each cell.

Example 13: Broadcast A Typed Scalar Note¶

const auto values = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{2, 10, -1});
const auto limit = pluss::note::make(std::int64_t{2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(values >= limit) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, true, false]

The result keeps the vector shape while changing dtype from Int64 to Bool.

Example 14: Higher Rank Is Preserved¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c", "d"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix > "b") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, dtype=Bool)
[
  [false, false], 
  [true, true]
]

Example 15: Native Dtypes And NaN¶

const auto reals = pluss::note::make(std::vector<double>{
    1.0, std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN(), 3.0});
const auto flags = pluss::note::make(std::vector<bool>{false, true, true});

std::cout << "NaN equality\n" << pluss::note::print(reals == reals) << '\n';
std::cout << "Bool order\n"
          << pluss::note::print(flags > pluss::note::make(false)) << '\n';

Output¶

NaN equality
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, false, true]
Bool order
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[false, true, true]

Example 16: Empty Comparison Preserves Empty Geometry¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 0});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(empty == empty) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 0], dim=2, numel=0, dtype=Bool)
[]

Example 17: Comparison Failures¶

const auto ints = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2});
const auto reals = pluss::note::make(std::vector<double>{1.0, 2.0});

try { (void)(ints == reals); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "mixed dtype: rejected\n"; }
try { (void)(ints == "2"); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "string against Int64: rejected\n"; }
try { (void)(ints == pluss::Note::undefined()); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "undefined: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

mixed dtype: rejected
string against Int64: rejected
undefined: rejected

Boolean Composition¶

&, |, and ^ pair Bool lanes under the shared shape rule. ~ negates every lane and preserves shape. Both operands of a binary Boolean expression must already be Bool Notes; no truthiness conversion is performed.

The operators are eager: both operands are evaluated before lanes are combined. They do not have the short-circuit behavior of scalar && and ||. Parenthesize comparisons and predicates in mixed expressions so the intended grouping remains obvious to readers.

Example 18: Combine Two Predicate Results¶

const auto names = pluss::note::make({"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"});
const auto has_a = names.contains("a");
const auto long_name = names.lengths_chars() >=
                       pluss::note::make(std::int64_t{5});

std::cout << "and\n" << pluss::note::print(has_a & long_name) << '\n';
std::cout << "or\n"  << pluss::note::print(has_a | long_name) << '\n';
std::cout << "xor\n" << pluss::note::print(has_a ^ long_name) << '\n';
std::cout << "not\n" << pluss::note::print(~has_a) << '\n';

Output¶

and
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[false, true, false]
or
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, true, true]
xor
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, false, true]
not
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[false, false, true]

Example 19: Broadcast A Boolean Scalar¶

const auto mask = pluss::note::make({true, true, false});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(mask & pluss::note::make(true)) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, true, false]

Example 20: Logical Failures¶

const auto mask = pluss::note::make({true, false, true});
try { (void)(mask & pluss::note::make({"x", "y", "z"})); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "non-Bool: rejected\n"; }

try {
  const auto row = pluss::note::make(
      std::vector<bool>{true, false, true},
      std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{1, 3});
  (void)(mask & row);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "shape mismatch: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

non-Bool: rejected
shape mismatch: rejected

Stream Insertion¶

operator<< writes the same default public representation as pluss::note::print(stream, note). It returns the stream, enabling normal chaining. Rendering does not expose mutable storage or change the Note.

Example 21: Write A Note Directly To A Stream¶

const auto names = pluss::note::make({"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"});
std::cout << names << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Ada", "Grace", "Linus"]
